label: early-position token-pair detector (b/i/3/m/d/s followed by s/b/v/n/j/2), diffuse
explanation: Sparse (about 1% of steps) and depends on combinations of tokens. About 60% of activation mass is in the original phase, concentrated at t=1-3 (peak at t=2), when the input is s, b, v, n, j or 2 and the previous token is b, i, 3, m, d or s (e.g. b b s at t=2 is one of the strongest). The other ~40% is in the copy phase, at the start (recall_idx 1-2, output often n or 2) and near the end of long sequences. It never fires at t=0 or on the delimiter step. The best single predicate (bigram at t=1-3) gets dev F1 0.33 (P 0.34, R 0.32, mass recall 0.39). Adding copy-phase clauses raises recall but lowers precision a lot. No coherent rule was found; the unit behaves like a distributed mix of token and position.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by phase (input phase: s, b, v, j; copy phase: n, 2, 1, k; delimiter step: ) and the previous input (most: b, 3, i, m, d, s; least: n, 2, q, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, L=4 & t=3, L=3 & t=2.
